description: One word a rep types, and the value the CRM already holds that it stands for. Nothing is invented here: the value is checked against the live masters before the row saves, and a value that does not exist is refused with the closest one named. Aliases are read only while the Search::Query::vocabulary switch is on, under Automations, so a table filled in before that switch is turned on changes nothing. Only the closed sets are reachable — a stage, a status, a product line, a group, a program, a person. Patient names, numbers and ids are matched as text by the index itself and need no row here.

fields.label: Term
fields.description: The word a rep types. Stored lower-cased with punctuation as a space, because that is how a typed query is read; a phrase of several words is allowed and is preferred over any shorter word inside it. A word that is already a value in its own right is refused, since two meanings for one word narrow nothing.

fields.label: Resolves To
fields.description: The value the term stands for, written the way the CRM shows it. It is resolved on save: unknown is refused with the nearest declared value named, and a value held in two different places is refused until one of them is chosen.

fields.label: Resolved
fields.description: What the value above was understood to be. Filled in on save and never typed. The row points at the record rather than at its spelling, so a value renamed later is followed rather than lost.
